gap: No result ChatGPT got states, for the number-pad boards that actually sell under $60, what each maker's size label means in keys and width next to its battery in both mAh and hours: Keychron's "100%" J5 is 435.93 mm wide with 3,750 mAh rated "up to 300 hours", Gamakay's "98%" TK101 is 101 keys, and Womier quotes 10,000 mAh for the X98.
standout_why: I opened the two cited pages (techgearden.com, kazsushibistro.com) and the top two results (keebkit.com, gearedgaming.com). None mentions the Keychron J5, Gamakay TK101, Womier X98, Attack Shark X98 or Rosewill S96. TechGearDen gives mAh for the AULA F99 (8,000) but no hours and no polling rate for any board. Kazsushibistro gives on/off hours only for a 75% AOC GK330 (55 h RGB on, 220 h off). KeebKit and Geared Gaming give no battery or polling figures. The table is new against those pages, but it is only half filled: the product pages on keychron.com, gamakay.com, womierkeyboard.com and attackshark.com returned HTTP 429 or failed on every attempt, so the J5, TK101 and Womier rows come from each store's own search record and the Attack Shark and Rosewill rows are unsourced. It informs the pick and does not decide it alone.
decides: It confirms the Keychron J5 as the honest overall pick on what the makers state: $44.99 at Keychron's US store, a true 100% layout, 1,000 Hz, QMK, and the only board here with both capacity and hours stated. The Gamakay TK101 ($47.99 through our link, 98% layout, 101 keys, gasket mount, hot-swappable) is the row we can link, and honestly wins only the compact, gasket-mount segment. That claim needs its width, battery and 2.4 GHz mode read from the product page first: the store text I read lists "Tri-mode connection" but names only Bluetooth 5.1 and USB-C. None of the seven keyboards we already list fits the question, since all are 75% boards with no number pad and all are above $60 through our link, so the page needs a new TK101 record or it is a skip. Two of ChatGPT's picks sit on the budget line: the Womier X98 is $84.99 at Womier's own store (ChatGPT's $56.99 was a Best Buy listing I did not open), and TechGearDen lists the AULA F99 at $63.99.
